name: Cryogenic vacuum extraction of soil and plant water for d2H/d18O analysis (18-slot manifold, 0.3 Pa, 90 C, liquid-nitrogen U-tube traps)
plain_name: Pull water out of soil samples under vacuum for isotope tracing
description: Frozen soil or plant samples in extraction tubes are evacuated to 0.3 Pa, then heated to 90 C in a water bath while the evaporated water is frozen in U-tubes immersed in liquid nitrogen; the recovered water is analysed for stable hydrogen and oxygen isotopes to trace water sources in ecohydrology.
keywords: Pull water out of soil samples under vacuum for isotope tracing

sources.citation: Orlowski N, Frede H-G, Brueggemann N, Breuer L (2013). Validation and application of a cryogenic vacuum extraction system for soil and plant water extraction for isotope analysis. J. Sens. Sens. Syst. 2, 179-193. doi:10.5194/jsss-2-179-2013

reported_equipment: Edwards RV5 two-stage rotary vane pump
Swagelok stainless-steel vacuum manifold with 18 extraction slots

requirements.rationale: The extraction runs under vacuum so water distils from the heated sample to the cold trap.
The validated procedure evacuates the line to 0.3 Pa before extraction; the authors note lower pressure may be needed for clay soils.
Samples are held at 90 C (363.15 K) for the whole extraction.
The evolved vapour is collected in liquid-nitrogen-cooled traps.
Extraction must run to completion to avoid fractionation; the validation runs lasted 180 min.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
